newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai B share index ends up in active trading.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai B share index ends up in active trading.

text.p: Shanghai's B share index ended up in active trading on Tuesday despite new rules banning securities rule violators from holding senior positions in the industry or from trading, brokers said.
The index inched up 0.362 points or 0.53 percent to 68.491 points on volume of 29.3 million shares worth US$13.0 million.

The rules, issued by the China Securities Regulatory Commission (CSRC), said company officials found to engage in insider trading and traders found to manipulate prices will be banned from the industry permanently or for several years.
Brokers said that active buying supported the market, with market sentiment good.
"We are seeing fresh capital flowing into the market, which improved market sentiment," one broker said.
Another broker said there was more buying than profit-taking at current levels because most investors view B share as being undervalued compared to their A share equivalents.
"The index will breach the current level soon given the strong market sentiment," he said.
All 43 B shares traded, with 23 up, five flat and 15 down.
Huangshan Tourism was the star after a recent period of consolidation, up $0.028 or 6.19 percent to $0.480 on volume of 4.6 million shares.
Clothing maker Shanghai Kaikai traded the most and became the second winner on institutional buying, gaining $0.014 or 3.95 percent to $0.368 on volume of 4.6 million shares.
Shanghai A shares reversed early losses caused by new rules due to an inflow of speculative hot money, brokers said.
The index rose 5.336 points or 0.48 percent to 1,116.792 points on volume of 840.5 million shares worth 8.3 billion yuan.
The SSE30 index edged up 1.871 points or 0.07 percent to 2,874.359 points.
Shanghai Fello was the star on institutional buying, soaring 0.88 yuan or 10.03 percent to 9.65 yuan on volume of 20.5 million shares.
